Hi @ROCm/miopen-reviewers  @averinevg,

I'm working at AMD on our developer ecosystem collaboration with Ultralytics, and I'd appreciate your help prioritizing an initial review of this PR.

**Why this matters:** We're working to improve the Ultralytics experience on Windows Radeon GPUs. In our investigation, PyTorch detected the Radeon GPU and YOLO inference worked, but YOLO training failed because MIOpen's HIPRTC compilation depended on host C++ standard-library headers that were unavailable in the Windows runtime environment.

**PR #13437 addresses this blocker at the MIOpen level**, without requiring changes to Ultralytics' training source code.

We've completed substantial validation:
- **Windows Radeon 8060S (gfx1151):** Genuine no-STL regression test passed, BatchNorm validated, and YOLO26n training completed successfully.
- **Linux gfx1100 and gfx1151:** Source-built MIOpen A/B validation passed, with no regressions in the tested workloads.
- **PR policy checks:** Passed, including the Unit Test check.

The remaining CI workflows — including pre-commit, Component CI, and TheRock CI — currently show `action_required`, apparently awaiting approval for an external contributor.

**Could someone with the appropriate permissions help approve the pending CI workflows and arrange an initial technical review?**

This fix would help remove a real training blocker for affected Windows Radeon users and support our broader efforts to make ROCm a more accessible platform for the Ultralytics developer community.

Happy to provide additional reproductions, testing, or fixes based on your feedback.

Thanks for your support!
@AIwork4me Thanks for addressing the comments! I've approved the CI workflows to run.

Hi @averinevg,

Thanks again for reviewing the changes and approving the CI workflows!

All four review threads have been addressed and resolved. The regression test has been migrated into MIOpen's existing gtest infrastructure.

I've also reviewed the latest CI results. All major workflows passed except **TheRock Multi-Arch CI**.

The failing `test_no_cross_artifact_overlaps` check reports 16 overlapping files between `profiler-hub` and `rocprofiler-systems` across 270 artifact archives.

None of these overlaps involve MIOpen files or components modified by this PR, so the failure appears unrelated to the proposed fix.

**Could you advise on the appropriate next step to unblock the PR?** Should this packaging issue be handled separately by the TheRock maintainers?

The MIOpen changes are ready for further technical review. Happy to address any additional feedback.

Thanks for your support!

Summary of the second-round updates (head `f0f330c4`, two commits on the latest develop `b8cf0e7b`):

- Merged the freestanding type-traits/utility fallbacks into `miopen_type_traits.hpp` / `miopen_utility.hpp` with `__has_include`-based selection; HIP < 7 handling dropped, separate freestanding files deleted.
- Renamed to `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` with the selection logic moved inside; `tensor_view.hpp` just includes it.
- `radix.hpp` now includes what it uses (`miopen_cstdint.hpp` + `miopen_type_traits.hpp`).
- The regression test compiles a trivial inline kernel (`miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp` style) exercising the added STL-like parts, with shorter comments and one-line assertions.

Fresh validation on Windows 11 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, ROCm 7.14.0 wheels): no-STL regression **PASS** (5 fresh hipRTC compiles under `-nostdinc`), unpatched-tree negative control **FAILs with the original signature**, BatchNorm training fwd/bwd vs CPU **PASS** (max err ≤ 9.5e-07), kthvalue **27/27**, YOLO26n COCO8 one-epoch training **PASS**. Historical Linux evidence is kept as supporting material in the PR description.

Ready for another look whenever you have time.

Hi @averinevg,

A quick follow-up: the final-HEAD Windows validation evidence for PR #13437 is now published and merged into our evidence repository:

https://github.com/AIwork4me/Ultralytics-Windows-ROCm-Training-RCA/tree/main/phase5_7/pr13437_final_head_f0f330c4

**Validated PR HEAD:** `f0f330c4`

The evidence includes:
- **HIPRTC no-STL regression:** PASS, with fresh kernel compilations and GPU execution.
- **Negative control:** Expected failure on the unpatched baseline, reproducing the original `'type_traits' file not found` error.
- **BatchNorm forward/backward:** PASS against a CPU reference.
- **kthvalue:** 27/27 PASS across FP32, FP16, and BF16.
- **YOLO26n:** One-epoch GPU training completed successfully on Windows gfx1151.
- **Reproducibility:** Source/binary provenance, raw logs, SHA256 manifests, and independent review records.

This was an evidence-only update. **No changes were made to the upstream PR branch.**

The new GitHub Actions runs are still showing `action_required`. Could you or another maintainer approve them so the final CI checks can run?

Thanks again for your guidance and continued review!

reviews.body: Thanks for the contribution! First pass below is an automated AI review.

@AIwork4me Second round: I left a few more inline comments, mostly about simplifying the headers and the test.

Could you also merge the latest develop? The TheRock Multi-Arch CI failure you mentioned is not related to this PR: develop failed the same way with the previous TheRock, and passes since it was updated.

title: MIOpen: make HIPRTC kernel includes self-contained without host STL
